module_summary: editor_file.c, editor_input.c, editor_menu.c and editor_rules.c are the classic uLaunchELF TextEditor (file open/save, pad virtual keyboard and USB keyboard entry, popup menus, cursor/row layout rules); the entry point TextEditor() lives in editor.c. The dashboard has its own editor (dash_editor.c) that the dashboard uses for every text file, so the classic one only survives behind a few classic entry points. elf.c holds the launch-argument store (.arg sidecars, editor buffers), ELF/KELF header classification, the MBR/xfrom payload loader and RunLoaderElf*, which copies the embedded loader ELF into memory and ExecPS2s it. embed_blobs.S .incbin-embeds exploit payloads, memory-card icons, prebuilt UDPFS/v1.0 network IRX and dashboard sound effects. ember.c validates the Ember PS1 emulator layout (<umbrella>/games/<Game>/image, bios.bin, ember.elf, staging ember.elf from a configured directory) and launches it with a keep-IOP handoff; ember_gameid.c parses a CUE sheet to find the data track and builds a PS1 game ID.

reusable_helpers.name: LaunchArgsLoadFromBuffer
reusable_helpers.what: parses a newline-separated argument buffer into the bounded launch-argument store

reusable_helpers.name: LaunchArgsLoadSidecarForExec
reusable_helpers.what: derives <exec>.arg from an executable path and loads it as launch arguments

reusable_helpers.name: classifyExecHeader
reusable_helpers.what: classifies a header buffer as MIPS ELF (1), encrypted KELF heuristic (2) or not executable (-1)

reusable_helpers.name: normalizeExecArg0Path
reusable_helpers.what: rewrites hddN:/part/path and usb/mass aliases into hddN:part:pfs:/path and massN:/path forms

reusable_helpers.name: RunEmbeddedLoader
reusable_helpers.what: copies PT_LOAD segments of an in-memory ELF, flushes caches and ExecPS2s it

reusable_helpers.name: copyElf
reusable_helpers.what: copies a file in 32 KB chunks and removes a partial destination on failure

reusable_helpers.name: appendFile
reusable_helpers.what: joins dir and file name with the separator style already used in dir, bounded

reusable_helpers.name: cueDataTrack
reusable_helpers.what: parses a CUE sheet for the first data track's BIN file, sector size and INDEX 01 offset

findings.title: Classic TextEditor (editor*.c) is superseded by dash_editor.c; route the remaining callers to dashTextEditor and delete it
findings.problem: dash_editor.c:3 says it replaces the classic TextEditor() wherever the dashboard opens text; every dashboard entry (dash_main.c:470-473, dash_browser.c:767,3003, dash_tools.c:1622, dash_files.c:324, dash_settings.c:3495, dash_hdd.c:953) uses dashTextEditor. The classic editor (editor.c plus the four files of this unit) is left only behind classic paths: executeBrowserSelection and the Misc_TextEditor branch of ExecuteMainAction (main_actions.c:231,771, reachable e.g. through Execute(igr_after_path) main.c:240), the classic filer menu (filer_browser.c:1554) and the hddHeaderTextEditor default, which dash_hdd.c:967 even restores to TextEditor after each use.
findings.fix: Point main_actions.c:231 and :771, filer_browser.c:1554 and the hddHeaderTextEditor default (hdd_header_injector.c:826, dash_hdd.c:967) at dashTextEditor (it already returns the same TEXTEDITOR_RESULT_* codes, see dash_main.c:515), move EditorSpecialChars/EditorSpecialCharCount (used by dash_widgets.c:54,68) next to dash_widgets.c, then delete editor.c, editor_file.c, editor_input.c, editor_menu.c, editor_rules.c and most of include/editor_private.h, and drop them from ps2.yaml:553-557. tests/test_editor_keyboard.py reads src/editor_input.c and must follow the table.
findings.benefit: MEASURED (raw/link/wLaunchELF-contrib-by-object.tsv): editor.o 28,860 + editor_input.o 12,536 + editor_file.o 3,308 + editor_menu.o 2,048 + editor_rules.o 1,332 = 48,084 bytes of ELF/RAM (18,868 of it .bss); ~2,000 source lines (688+705+324+229+123 minus the moved table).
findings.evidence: Grep TextEditor( over src: callers only main_actions.c:231,771, filer_browser.c:1554, hdd_header_injector.c:826 (pointer), dash_hdd.c:967 (pointer restore); every dash_* caller uses dashTextEditor/dashOpenTextEditor. dashRunMisc (dash_main.c:451-495) handles Misc_TextEditor and Misc_FileBrowser before runMiscCommand. NOT verified: whether the classic filer menu (filer_browser.c) and ExecuteMainAction's Misc_TextEditor/FileBrowser branches are still reachable in practice (IGR after-path, launch keys); that is why confidence is Low. EditorSpecialChars use: dash_widgets.c:12,54,68. Build list ps2.yaml:553-557.

findings.title: Classic editor leaks the whole text buffer on every inserted character: free() is swallowed into a comment
findings.problem: In both insert paths the line that should free the old buffer reads as one comment ('//memset(...); // 256 ...  free(TextBuffer[Active_Window]);'), so the next line overwrites TextBuffer[Active_Window] with a new malloc and the old block (TextSize+ins1+256 bytes) is lost on every typed char, Return, Tab or Paste. Typing 100 characters into a 100 KB file leaks ~10 MB; when malloc then returns NULL, strcpy at :374/:649 writes through NULL. The delete path (:387, :664) shows the intended separate free().
findings.fix: Put free(TextBuffer[Active_Window]) back on its own line in both places (or, simpler, realloc the buffer once instead of the TMP copy dance); if the classic editor is deleted (finding 1) this goes with it.
findings.benefit: Fixes an unbounded heap leak per keystroke in the classic editor (INFERRED arithmetic: TextSize+ins1+256 bytes per insert).
findings.evidence: Read editor_input.c:369-375 and 644-650: line 372 and 647 each contain the memset comment followed on the same line by the free() call, all after '//'. Line 373/648 assigns a fresh malloc to TextBuffer[Active_Window] without freeing. Compare delete case :386-389 / :663-666 where memset comment and free() are separate lines. Reachability of the classic editor: see finding 1 (main_actions.c:231,771, filer_browser.c:1554).

findings.title: editor_input.c: pad and USB-keyboard handlers copy the same mark, clipboard, return-key, char-insert and apply-operation blocks
findings.problem: editorVirtualKeyboardEntry and editorKeyboardEntry repeat the same code: mark-range normalise (7 copies of ~7 lines), copy-to-clipboard malloc+loop (4 copies), MARK toggle (2x13 lines), PASTE setup (2x8), RETURN ins1..ins5 table (2x19 lines), the buffer-apply switch (369-426 vs 644-696, ~50 lines) and the single-char insert setup, which editorPrepareSingleCharInsert (153-167) already implements but 628-639 re-inlines.
findings.fix: If the classic editor stays: call editorPrepareSingleCharInsert at 628-639, and move the shared blocks into a few static helpers (normalise mark, copy mark to clipboard, set return ins values, apply Operation with the inserted char as parameter) called from both handlers.
findings.justification: The same blocks occur 2 to 7 times in one file; each helper replaces at least two copies, so the file shrinks.
findings.benefit: ~110 source lines removed (INFERRED from the cited ranges: apply block ~50, return table ~19, mark/clip copies ~30, char insert ~11); a few hundred bytes of .text (INFERRED). Moot if finding 1 is done.
findings.evidence: Read all of editor_input.c. dupes-blocks.tsv leads confirmed: 217-231==585-599, 253-269==274-290==548-564, 257-269==531-543, 333-352==606-625, 381-408==658-685. 628-639 is textually the body of editorPrepareSingleCharInsert 155-166. editorPrepareSingleCharInsert is static and only called at :355.

findings.title: Copy before genFixPath is a dead store (genFixPath overwrites it); the fix-or-raw-path fallback is hand-written in 10 places
findings.problem: genFixPath always starts with strcpy(gen_path, uLE_path) (filer.c:956), so the strncpy done just before it in editor_file.c:80-81, 219-220, 285-286 and elf.c:90 is overwritten every time. The 'if genFixPath fails, copy the raw path' fallback is then repeated by hand at every listed site (elf.c even has two helpers, launchArgsCopyPath and launchArgsMakeOpenPath, only for it).
findings.fix: Delete the pre-copies. Optionally make genFixPath itself copy the raw path on failure (or add one genFixPathOrRaw in filer.c) and drop the per-site fallbacks and elf.c's launchArgsCopyPath/launchArgsMakeOpenPath.
findings.justification: One shared fallback replaces ten 2-4 line copies and two elf.c helpers, so the net is fewer lines.
findings.benefit: ~8 lines of dead stores; ~30 lines with the shared fallback (INFERRED from the cited ranges).
findings.evidence: Read filer.c:946-986: gen_path is written unconditionally at :956 before any return. Grep 'if (genFixPath(...) < 0)' over src: fallback-to-raw at editor_file.c:82,221,287, elf.c:91, dash_editor.c:315, hdd_header_injector.c:698,722,761,800, main_exploit_installer.c:1513; other sites return an error instead. launchArgsCopyPath callers: only elf.c:90,92; launchArgsMakeOpenPath: elf.c:211,247.

findings.title: editor_file.c: editorSave/editorSaveAs repeat the write block with a never-true CRLF branch; 1.5 s busy-wait loop pasted 5 times
findings.problem: The open/write/close/unmountParty block is duplicated between editorSave and editorSaveAs. Its test TextBuffer[Win][TextSize[Win]] == '\n' reads the terminator slot (the buffer is zeroed at load, 107/119, and every edit re-terminates with strcpy/strcat at TextSize), so the TextSize-1 branch at 229-230 and 295-296 never runs. The 'WaitTime = Timer(); while (Timer() < WaitTime + 1500);' result delay is copied five times in this file.
findings.fix: Move the write block into one static helper used by both functions, write TextSize bytes unconditionally, and replace the five delay loops with one static helper (or a single delay at the common exit).
findings.justification: The helpers each replace two to five identical copies, so the file gets shorter.
findings.benefit: ~22 source lines removed (INFERRED: 10 from the write block, 2x2 dead branch, 8 from the delay copies).
findings.evidence: Read editor_file.c fully. Grep 'while (Timer() < WaitTime +' over src: only the 5 editor_file.c sites. The never-true claim is INFERRED from the buffer handling read in editor_file.c:105-143 and editor_input.c:369-426,644-696 (strings stay NUL-terminated at TextSize); not traced for every edit sequence.

findings.title: Classic editor leftovers: unused HFONTS, always-true conditions, commented-out code
findings.problem: HFONTS (editor_input.c:7, extern editor_private.h:92) has no user; gui.c:149 has its own local HFONTS. In editorMenu, Menu_Sel < NUM_MENU (54, 61, 110) is always true because NEW/OPEN/EXIT are never disabled; in editorSelectWindow the else-if Window[i][OPENED] (193) is always true there, and Window_Sel <= 10 (199) always holds (0..9). Lines 191, 278-281 and the memset comment lines in editor_input.c are dead commented-out code.
findings.fix: Delete HFONTS and its extern, drop the always-true conditions (plain else at 193), and delete the commented-out lines.
findings.benefit: 4 bytes .rodata MEASURED (BUILD-EVIDENCE.md:160 lists editor_input.o HFONTS as unreferenced but kept); ~14 source lines.
findings.evidence: grep -w HFONTS over the repo: editor_input.c:7, editor_private.h:92, and gui.c:149-377 which declares its own const local. editor_menu.c:30-43 only ever disables CLOSE, SAVE, SAVE_AS, WINDOWS, LAUNCH_WITH_ARGS, so the loop at 45-47 stops below NUM_MENU. Window_Sel wraps 0..9 at 161-166.

findings.title: editor_rules.c: the same row-find loop is written four times
findings.problem: Home, End, Line/Page Up and Line/Page Down each run the identical loop that accumulates Editor_nRowsWidth until it passes Editor_Cur+1 to find the cursor row.
findings.fix: Compute the cursor row index and its cumulative end once before the four branches (or in one static helper) and reuse it.
findings.justification: One computation replaces four identical loops, net fewer lines.
findings.benefit: ~15 source lines (INFERRED from the four 6-line ranges); negligible .text.
findings.evidence: Read editor_rules.c 1-123; the four loops are textually identical apart from the comment.

findings.title: elf.c isElfPayload/isLikelyEncryptedPayload re-implement classifyExecHeader; getMbrOpenPath re-inlines isHddPartyPath
findings.problem: isElfPayload and isLikelyEncryptedPayload repeat the MIPS-ELF check and the 'byte0==0x01, byte2==0x00' KELF heuristic of classifyExecHeader in the same file. The test '!isElfPayload && encrypted' at 695 is redundant: a buffer starting with 0x01 can never start with 0x7F 'ELF'. getMbrOpenPath line 623 spells out isHddPartyPath (357-360) instead of calling it.
findings.fix: Delete isElfPayload and isLikelyEncryptedPayload and use classifyExecHeader(payload, payload_size) == 2 at 694-695; call isHddPartyPath at 623.
findings.benefit: ~19 source lines removed (INFERRED from 588-604 plus 693-695); some bytes of .text in the XFROM build.
findings.evidence: Read elf.c fully. grep -w isElfPayload / isLikelyEncryptedPayload over the repo: only elf.c definitions and the uses at 694-695. classifyExecHeader and isHddPartyPath are defined outside #ifdef XFROM (300, 357), so they are visible inside the XFROM block. XFROM is always defined (ps2.yaml:618).

findings.title: elf.c launchArgSource is written but never read (1 KB .bss and a dead source parameter chain)
findings.problem: launchArgSource[MAX_PATH] is only cleared (41) and filled (151-154); no code reads it. The source argument of launchArgsFinishParse and launchArgsReadFromFd exists only to fill it, and the source parameter of LaunchArgsLoadFromBuffer feeds nothing else.
findings.fix: Delete launchArgSource, its clear and copy, and the source parameter of the two static helpers; optionally drop source from LaunchArgsLoadFromBuffer and its six callers.
findings.benefit: 1,025 bytes .bss (INFERRED: char[MAX_PATH], MAX_PATH = 1025 in launchelf.h:204); ~6 lines.
findings.evidence: grep -w launchArgSource over the repo: elf.c:35, 41, 152, 153 only (all writes). LaunchArgsLoadFromBuffer callers: dash_editor.c:1167, dash_main.c:639, ember.c:354, editor.c:348, neutrino_iso.c:274; LaunchArgsLoadFromFile: dash_browser.c:2568, filer_browser.c:1568. Tests stub LaunchArgsLoadFromBuffer with the source parameter (test_ember_retrogem_handoff.py:30, test_launch_iop_override.py:99, test_neutrino_menu_audio.py:61).

findings.title: WLE_PS2BUILD is always defined: the #else branches for the retired Makefile build are dead
findings.problem: ps2.yaml is the only build (legacy Makefile retired) and defines WLE_PS2BUILD (ps2.yaml:615); the DS34 variant keeps it (configure_ds34.py:36). The two #else branches declaring bin2s-style loader_elf/wle_igr_elf symbols can no longer be compiled.
findings.fix: Keep the PS2BUILD declarations, delete the #ifdef/#else/#endif and the else branches; then the WLE_PS2BUILD define in ps2.yaml and configure_ds34.py can go too (configure_ds34 would anchor its DS34 insertion on another line).
findings.benefit: ~10 source lines; no ELF change (INFERRED: preprocessor only).
findings.evidence: grep -rn WLE_PS2BUILD over the repo: elf.c:15, mmce_igr.c:16, ps2.yaml:615, configure_ds34.py:36. No Makefile exists (brief section 2, docs/BUILDING.md:22).

findings.title: elf.c small leftovers: MAX_PATH redefinition, unreachable else branches after a repeated test, stray braces, stale (void)exec_kind
findings.problem: elf.c:11 #defines MAX_PATH 1025 after including launchelf.h, which already has the enum MAX_PATH = 1025 (launchelf.h:204). The outer if at 762 already requires !strncmp(filename, "pfs0:", 5), so the same test at 775 is always true and 777-779 is unreachable; likewise 787 requires the dvr_pfs_name prefix, making 799-801 unreachable. The extra block braces at 763/771 serve nothing, and (void)exec_kind at 819 is stale since exec_kind is used at 749.
findings.fix: Delete the #define, keep only the true branches of the repeated tests, drop the extra braces and the (void) cast.
findings.benefit: ~13 source lines; no ELF change expected (INFERRED: the compiler already folds the repeated tests).
findings.evidence: grep 'define MAX_PATH' over the repo: only elf.c:11 and kelf_signer.c:21 in production; enum at include/launchelf.h:204. Read elf.c:728-831.

findings.title: ember.c copyElf duplicates psu_functions.c psu_backup_copy_bytes (copy file, delete partial output)
findings.problem: Both static functions open a source, create/truncate a destination, copy in a heap buffer until EOF, check each write, close both and genRemove the destination on failure (~30 of their lines do the same thing). They differ only in buffer size (32 KB vs PSU_COPY_BUFFER), memalign vs malloc, openPathForRead vs genOpen for the source and the return convention.
findings.fix: Keep one of them as a shared non-static helper (for example psu_backup_copy_bytes, returning 0/negative) and call it from ensureLocalEmber; delete copyElf.
findings.justification: Two real copies exist; sharing one removes ~35 lines net.
findings.benefit: ~35 source lines and a few hundred bytes of .text (INFERRED; ember.o total is 4,092 bytes MEASURED in wLaunchELF-contrib-by-object.tsv).
findings.evidence: Read ember.c:209-246 and psu_functions.c:127-162. Grep for other copy-file helpers ('int .*copy.*(const char *, const char *') found also filer_copy.c:90 copyBufferSize (filer pipeline, different shape) and hdd_header_injector.c PFS copies; not checked whether those can also share. copyElf has one caller (ember.c:289); whether source paths need openPathForRead's device handling was not verified.

findings.title: embed_blobs.S: three embed macros differ only in the .incbin arguments
findings.problem: EMBED_FILE, EMBED_SLICE and EMBED_TAIL are the same 11-line macro body; only the .incbin operand list differs (file / file,off,len / file,off).
findings.fix: Keep one macro that takes the symbol and a variadic .incbin operand list (EMBED(sym, ...) with .incbin __VA_ARGS__) and use it for all 26 entries.
findings.benefit: ~22 source lines; no ELF change (INFERRED: same directives emitted).
findings.evidence: Read embed_blobs.S 1-91. All 26 embedded symbols have users (grep: config.c, init.c, dash_sound.c, main_exploit_installer.c), so none can be dropped; md5 shows exploits/list.icn and res/memory-card/list.icn differ, so no duplicate blob. Variadic macros in .S rely on the C preprocessor used for .S files (INFERRED, not built).
